articles.title: 'This too shall pass': Sherfane Rutherford evokes Virat Kohli memory with X post on Babar Azam
articles.summary: After Babar Azam once again failed to score big in the Tri-series finals, WI batter Sherfane Rutherford tweeted a heartfelt message for the former Pak skippe...
articles.body:
Sherfane Rutherford posted a message of support for Babar Azam on X, using the same line Babar once sent to Virat Kohli.

Babar's tweet in July 2022 came after Kohli fell for 16 against England at Lord's, and Kohli thanked him in a public reply.

Babar is under pressure for a lack of big scores, with Pakistan 's batting coach saying the team will continue to back him.

Sherfane Rutherford shows support for Babar Azam, evokes Virat Kohli memory

The pressure on Babar Azam continues to mount as he once again failed to show up for his country in the Tri-series final against Sri Lanka. The former all-format skipper fell for a five-ball duck as Pakistan nearly lost the tournament. It also marked his seventh innings without a fifty since scoring an uneventful 69 against the Aussies in May.

This period is an unseemly lean patch for Babar Azam, a player who was once touted as an equal to the Fab 4. However, Pakistan batting coach Mike Smith continues to remain on Azam's side. He quickly stated that the management would continue to back the batter. Smith wasn't the only one who extended their support to Azam.

West Indies batter Sherfane Rutherford was also quick to show his support for Babar on X, borrowing a line the Pakistan batter himself used for Virat Kohli in 2022. Rutherford posted the message with the hashtag #BabarAzam at a time when Babar is facing questions over a lack of big scores.

Rutherford kept his message short and informal, and it needed no further explanation for anyone who remembers the original. "This too shall pass; stay strong, buddy," Rutherford wrote .

It is not the first time Rutherford has spoken up for Babar in public. After the 2021 T20 World Cup final, he said he was "shocked" that Babar was not named Player of the Tournament.

What was Babar Azam's 2022 message to Virat Kohli, and how did Kohli respond?

Babar sent his message in July 2022, a day after Kohli fell for 16 in the second ODI against England at Lord's. India lost that match by 100 runs, and Kohli had not scored an international hundred since November 2019. Babar posted a photo of the two of them together, with a short caption. "This too shall pass. Stay strong. #ViratKohli," Babar wrote.

Kohli replied on his own X account a couple of days later, thanking Babar and wishing him well. "Thank you. Keep shining and rising. Wish you all the best 👏," Kohli wrote.

Babar later explained why he had posted it. "As a sportsperson, anyone can go through such a time," he said, adding that he hoped the message might give Kohli some support.

Why 'This too shall pass' now means more for Babar Azam

The line quickly became a two-way gesture. In October 2022, after Babar was dismissed for a duck against India at the T20 World Cup, Danish Sait tweeted, "Babar, this too shall pass", and the phrase was thrown back at him for months.

Rutherford's message is the opposite of that. It comes from a fellow international player, and it is a plain show of support at a point when most of the noise around Babar is critical. Kohli's lean patch ended that September, when he scored his first international hundred in almost three years against Afghanistan at the Asia Cup.

Babar has shown in the PSL this year that he can still score heavily. Doing the same for Pakistan in the coming matches is the only reply that will settle the argument, and a message like Rutherford's at least shows he has support in the dressing room and beyond it.

articles.title: Tension and clashes as hundreds of thousands protest again in France
articles.summary: Authorities say 320,000 march on third consecutive weekend of demonstrations over cost of living and state of schools.
articles.body:
Police have fired tear gas at protesters in Paris and Lyon as hundreds of thousands of mostly young people marched across France over the cost of living and the state of the country’s schools.

Saturday’s rallies were the third consecutive weekend of demonstrations in France.

A coalition of youth organisations and unions representing high school and university students said nearly half a million people took part, including 200,000 in Paris. The authorities put the nationwide turnout at 320,000, including 70,000 in the capital.

Marches in the capital began peacefully, but turned violent as protesters gathered near the point where the main march was due to end on Saturday. Bins and street furniture were set alight, and plumes of smoke could be seen rising over the city.

“What we’ve been seeing … is the police firing a lot of tear gas into this crowd,” said Al Jazeera’s Natacha Butler, reporting from Paris, adding that her team “had to move out of the way because it was simply too much for us to breathe”.

Riot police warned over loudspeakers that they would fire more tear gas if protesters did not clear the street. Medics carried away people who had been injured, while some protesters raised their hands to show police they meant no harm.

Dozens of masked people dressed in black also used hammers to pry up paving stones and hurl them at police on the outskirts of Paris, the AFP news agency reported. At least one incendiary device was also thrown at security forces, who responded with tear gas and baton charges.

France’s Ministry of Interior said at least 290 people nationwide had so far been arrested.

Butler said most protesters condemned the violence, but many blamed the government for failing to listen to them.

“You really get a sense with people who have come into the street again and again over the past few weeks that they simply don’t believe the government any more. That trust has gone,” she said.

The government says it has heard the protesters. Prime Minister Sebastien Lecornu has held several meetings with student unions this week and is looking at measures to ease the cost of living.

About 70,000 police and gendarmes were deployed across the country, and Interior Minister Laurent Nunez warned of a “very high risk” of disorder, especially after dark on Halloween.

The main Paris march was moved to the city’s eastern edge after a last-minute court battle, and unaccompanied minors faced a 9pm (20:00 GMT) curfew around the Champs-Elysees.

The movement began last month with high school students protesting against neglected buildings, teacher shortages and a university admissions system seen as unfair to disadvantaged students. Labour unions have since joined.

On October 17 , protests drew more than 500,000 people and turned into some of France’s worst rioting in years, according to government estimates, with shops in Paris looted.

Meanwhile, protests have taken place in other cities across Europe.

On Saturday, young people in Germany were the latest to join the fray.

Thousands rallied while police in Cologne used water cannon to break up large crowds protesting against rising costs, education cuts and plans for military conscription. Organisers said 170,000 people had registered for demonstrations in more than 30 cities.

In Barcelona, Spain, regional police prepared their highest alert level after rioting on October 24 led to about 130 arrests, mostly of minors.

Italian police were also on alert after clashes in Milan, Turin and Bologna.

articles.summary: Pyare Khan, Maharashtra Minorities Commission chair, files ₹50 crore defamation suits against five over protest placards; court issues notices in Nagpur.
articles.body: Nagpur: Maharashtra State Minorities Commission chairman Pyare Khan has filed a civil defamation suit seeking damages of ₹50 crore each from five individuals, alleging they tarnished his reputation through a public protest.
